Smoked salmon & poached eggs

Thick toast, runny yolks, kimchi on the side.

Serves 215 minEasy

Ingredients

  • 2 thick slices sourdough
  • 2 tbsp cream cheese or butter
  • 100 g (3½ oz) smoked salmon
  • 4 very fresh eggs
  • 1 tbsp white vinegar
  • Black pepper and a pinch of chili flakes or paprika
  • Kimchi, to serve (optional)

Directions

  1. Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer, with small bubbles only, and add the vinegar.
  2. Crack each egg into its own small cup. Stir the water to make a slow swirl and slide the eggs in one at a time.
  3. Poach for 3 minutes for a runny yolk. Meanwhile, toast the bread.
  4. Spread the toast with cream cheese and drape the smoked salmon over it.
  5. Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon, let them drain for a moment on paper towel, and set two on each toast.
  6. Finish with black pepper and chili. Serve with kimchi on the side.

Creamy tomato chicken spaghetti

A weeknight pan sauce with roasted peppers.

Serves 435 minEasy

Ingredients

  • 2 large chicken breasts, sliced in half horizontally
  • 1 tsp paprika, salt and pepper
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • ½ cup (70 g) roasted red peppers or sun-dried tomatoes, chopped
  • 1 cup (240 ml) chicken stock
  • ¾ cup (180 ml) heavy cream
  • ½ cup (40 g) grated parmesan
  • 300 g (10 oz) spaghetti
  • Fresh basil or parsley

Directions

  1. Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Save ½ cup of the pasta water, then drain.
  2. Season the chicken with paprika, salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
  3. Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes per side, until golden and 74 °C (165 °F) inside. Set it aside on a plate.
  4. Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and peppers and cook for 1 minute, scraping up the browned bits.
  5. Pour in the stock and simmer for 3 minutes, then stir in the cream and parmesan until smooth.
  6. Return the chicken to the pan and spoon the sauce over it for 2 minutes. Loosen with pasta water if needed.
  7. Serve the chicken and sauce over the spaghetti, topped with fresh herbs.

Strawberry crêpes

Fresh berries, a quick sauce, a dusting of sugar.

Makes 830 minEasy

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (125 g) plain flour
  • 2 eggs
  • 1¼ cups (300 ml) milk
  • 2 tbsp melted butter, plus more for the pan
  • 1 tbsp sugar and a pinch of salt
  • 450 g (1 lb) strawberries
  • 2 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp lemon juice, for the sauce
  • Powdered sugar, to finish

Directions

  1. Whisk the flour, sugar, salt, eggs, milk and melted butter into a smooth, thin batter. Rest it for 10 minutes.
  2. For the sauce, chop a third of the strawberries and simmer them with the sugar and lemon juice for 5–7 minutes, until syrupy. Slice the rest.
  3. Heat a 20 cm (8 in) non-stick pan over medium heat and brush it with butter.
  4. Pour in about ¼ cup of batter and tilt the pan to coat the base. Cook for 1 minute, until the edges lift, then flip and cook for 30 seconds.
  5. Stack the finished crêpes on a plate and repeat with the rest of the batter.
  6. Fill or fold each crêpe with sliced strawberries, drizzle with the sauce and dust with powdered sugar.

Big weekend breakfast

Eggs, sausage, fruit and a green juice.

Serves 225 minEasy

Ingredients

  • 4 breakfast sausages
  • 4 eggs and 1 tbsp butter
  • Salt and pepper
  • 2 wedges of watermelon
  • ½ ripe papaya, peeled and sliced
  • For the juice: 2 handfuls spinach, 1 green apple, ½ cucumber, juice of ½ lemon, 1 cm ginger, ½ cup (120 ml) cold water

Directions

  1. Cook the sausages in a skillet over medium heat for 12–15 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through.
  2. Meanwhile, slice the watermelon and papaya and arrange them on the plates.
  3. For the juice, blend all the juice ingredients until smooth. Strain it if you prefer it thinner.
  4. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low heat.
  5. Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula. Take them off the heat while they are still slightly glossy.
  6. Plate the eggs and sausages beside the fruit and serve with the green juice.

Salmon with sweet potato mash

Green beans, lemon and a light pan sauce.

Serves 240 minMedium

Ingredients

  • 2 salmon fillets, about 150 g (5 oz) each
  • 2 medium sweet potatoes (about 600 g), peeled and cubed
  • 3 tbsp butter, divided
  • 200 g (7 oz) green beans, trimmed
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 1 lemon
  • Salt and pepper

Directions

  1. Boil the sweet potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until soft. Drain and mash with 1 tbsp butter, salt and pepper.
  2. Blanch the green beans in boiling salted water for 3 minutes, then drain.
  3. Pat the salmon dry and season it well. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
  4. Cook the salmon skin-side down for 4–5 minutes, until crisp, then flip and cook 2–3 minutes more. Move it to the plates.
  5. Lower the heat. Add the remaining butter and the garlic, then the juice of half the lemon. Toss the beans in this sauce for 1 minute.
  6. Serve the salmon with the mash and beans, spoon the pan sauce over, and add a lemon wedge.

Garlic butter escargot

Herbs, butter and bread to mop it all up.

Serves 4 as a starter25 minEasy

Ingredients

  • 24 canned escargots, drained and rinsed
  • 115 g (½ cup) unsalted butter, softened
  • 4 garlic cloves, finely minced
  • 1 small shallot, finely minced
  • 2 tbsp chopped parsley
  • 1 tbsp dry white wine (optional)
  • Salt and pepper
  • Baguette and lemon, to serve

Directions

  1. Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).
  2. Mash the butter with the garlic, shallot, parsley, wine, a pinch of salt and some pepper.
  3. Place one escargot in each well of an escargot dish. A small baking dish works too.
  4. Top each escargot with a generous spoonful of the garlic butter.
  5. Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the butter is bubbling and fragrant.
  6. Serve hot with sliced baguette for the butter and lemon wedges on the side.

Fresh spring rolls

Rice paper, crunchy vegetables, herbs.

Makes 830 minEasy

Ingredients

  • 8 rice paper sheets, 22 cm (8½ in)
  • 60 g (2 oz) rice vermicelli
  • 16 cooked shrimp, halved lengthwise (optional)
  • 1 carrot and ½ cucumber, cut into thin sticks
  • 8 soft lettuce leaves
  • A handful each of mint and cilantro
  • For the dip: 3 tbsp peanut butter, 1 tbsp hoisin, 1 tbsp lime juice, warm water to thin

Directions

  1. Cook the vermicelli as the packet says, rinse it under cold water and drain well.
  2. Whisk the dip ingredients together, adding warm water until the dip is pourable.
  3. Dip one rice paper sheet in warm water for 2–3 seconds and lay it on a damp board. It softens as you work.
  4. Lay shrimp along the lower third, then lettuce, noodles, carrot, cucumber and herbs on top.
  5. Fold in the sides, then roll it up tightly from the bottom. Repeat with the rest.
  6. Serve with the peanut dip. If you make them ahead, cover them with a damp towel for up to 2 hours.
